predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by the Hamdanid dynasty and the Fatimid Caliphate. Al-Rahba, the first Mirdasid seat, is held by the Uqaylids on the Qirwash page until 1014 (uqaylid-dynasty).

capitals.name: Aleppo
capitals.note: Salih entered the citadel in September 1025.

capitals.name: al-Rahba (Mayadin)
capitals.note: After Aleppo fell in 1038 Thimal "departed the city for the Jazira" and "retained the Mesopotamian portion of Mirdasid emirate"; al-Dizbari "was unable to take al-Rahba". The page names no seat for 1038-1039; al-Rahba, the first Mirdasid seat and the holding that stayed, is read as the capital until Raqqa in 1040.

capitals.name: Raqqa
capitals.note: After Aleppo fell to al-Dizbari in 1038 Thimal fled to the Jazira; inheriting Raqqa and Rafiqa in 1039/40 "He made Raqqa his capital".

capitals.name: Aleppo
capitals.note: Thimal entered Aleppo on 22 February 1042. He stepped down on 23 January 1058 and took up residence in Cairo; no seat is named for 1058-1059 (the emirate held no land the pages name in 1059), so no capital is given for those years.

capitals.name: Aleppo
capitals.note: Mahmud ibn Nasr seized Aleppo in September 1060; Thimal regained it on 23 April 1061 (reached its gates in January 1061); Atiyya gave it up to Mahmud in 1065; it stays Mirdasid to June 1080.

rulers.note: killed in battle against Anushtakin in 1038

rulers.name: Thimal ibn Salih (Mu'izz al-Dawla)
rulers.note: infobox 1042-1062; stepped down on 23 January 1058, recovered Aleppo on 23 April 1061, died 28 November 1062

rulers.name: Mahmud ibn Nasr (Shihab al-Dawla)
rulers.note: also held Aleppo from September 1060 to April 1061; "a vassal of the Seljuk sultan"; died 1075

rulers.name: Sabiq ibn Mahmud
rulers.note: ceded the emirate to Muslim ibn Quraysh in 1080

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mirdasid row): Salih "took the Euphrates fortress" al-Rahba in 1008, escaped from Aleppo's prison on 3 July 1014 and made al-Rahba his capital. No area on the page.

New keyframe: Manbij and Balis "gained in the years after 1014" (Mirdasid page: 'In the following years'; Salih page: "by 1022"), no year on either page, so 1015 is bridging inside 1014-1022 (reopened 2026-10-19).

correction.text: al-Rahba, Manbij, Balis, Raqqa and al-Rafiqa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "By 1022 he had added Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to his Jaziran realm."

correction.text: the Euphrates towns, Aleppo and the central Syrian domains

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Aleppo's citadel breached by 30 June 1025; "Homs, Baalbek, Sidon, Rafaniyya, Hisn Ibn Akkar" taken on his return from Palestine in 1025. The widest extent, an emirate from the Euphrates to the Lebanese coast.

correction.text: al-Rahba, Manbij, Balis, Raqqa and Aleppo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after al-Uqhuwana "the Fatimids conquered Sidon, Baalbek, Homs, Rafaniyya, and Hisn Ibn Akkar from Salih's deputies"; Nasr held Aleppo. The Mirdasid page says the Mirdasids "had also since lost control of Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to the Numayrids" without a year; Raqqa stays drawn to 1037 and the loss is written as 1038 (bridging).

New keyframe: al-Dizbari "had captured" Aleppo by June or July 1038 and Manbij and Balis were taken too; Thimal "fled to the Jazira" and Raqqa and Rafiqa were lost to the Numayrids (bridging, between 1022 and 1039/40).
New keyframe: Raqqa and Rafiqa inherited by Thimal's wife and entrusted to him in 1039/40; "He made Raqqa his capital."

New keyframe: Thimal entered Aleppo on 22 February 1042 and took the citadel after a seven-month siege. Raqqa is held to 1056 (Numayrid page: "In April 1056, after Thimal rejected Mani's demand to withdraw from Raqqa, hostilities broke out").

correction.text: al-Rahba and Aleppo; Raqqa lost to the Numayrids in October 1057

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19): Numayrid page: "al-Basasiri captured Raqqa from Thimal and transferred it to Mani' in October 1057" (Ibn Shaddad: Thimal "handed over both Raqqa and al-Rafiqah to Mani' due to military pressure"); Mani' has Raqqa either way.

correction.text: al-Rahba, the only Mirdasid holding the pages name after Thimal stepped down

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19): Thimal "stepped down on 23 January 1058", Aleppo passes to the Fatimid governor Ibn Mulhim and Thimal lives in Cairo. The Fatimid grant of Acre, Beirut and Jubayl is NOT drawn: the Thimal page calls it "evidently a tributary arrangement, as he did not exercise control over them" and the Fatimids "stripped Thimal of his holdings along the Syrian coast" after September 1060. al-Rahba is read as still Mirdasid until the Numayrid page's 1059 capture. The year 1059 has no keyframe: no Mirdasid land is named between al-Rahba's loss in 1059 and Mahmud's seizure of Aleppo in September 1060.

correction.text: Aleppo, seized by Mahmud ibn Nasr in September 1060

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19): Mahmud ibn Nasr seized Aleppo in September 1060; "Taken by Mahmud in 1060". The coast is not drawn (see 1058).
New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19): "Regained by Thimal in 1061" (23 April); "In August, Atiyya retook al-Rahba for Thimal". Raqqa is still Numayrid (Mani').

New keyframe (review fix 2026-10-19): Numayrid page: "Thimal's brother, Atiyya ibn Salih, took over Raqqa in 1062"; Aleppo (given up by Atiyya in 1065 to Mahmud, internal) stays Mirdasid to June 1080; no page dates a later loss of al-Rahba or Raqqa, so both are held to 1079 as bridging.
New keyframe: "in 1080, prompted by Sabiq, the Uqaylid emir of Mosul, Sharaf al-Dawla Muslim, took over Aleppo"; the dynasty ends in June 1080.

ledger.note: 1014: Salih ibn Mirdas escapes prison and founds the Mirdasid emirate. 'He escaped on 3 July 1014' and rallied his tribesmen at Marj Dabiq; he had 'taken the Euphrates fortress' al-Rahba in 1008 (infobox 1014-1080, capital al-Rahba 1014-1024).

1015: Manbij and Balis. 'Manbij and Balis: gained in the years after 1014. Lost to Anushtakin in 1038.' The Mirdasid page gives no year ('In the following years') and the Salih page says only "by 1022" (both reopened 2026-10-19); 1015 is bridging inside 1014-1022.

1022: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa. 'By 1022 he had added Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to his Jaziran realm.' The page does not name the previous holder; the Numayrid page has Waththab take Raqqa from its Hamdanid governor in 1007 and the Mirdasid page says the Mirdasids "had also since lost control of Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to the Numayrids", so the Numayrids are read as the loser.

region.text: Homs, Baalbek, Sidon, Rafaniyya and Hisn Ibn Akkar

ledger.note: 1025: the central Syrian domains. 'Homs, Baalbek, Sidon, Rafaniyya, Hisn Ibn Akkar: Taken on his return from Palestine in 1025.'

region.text: Aleppo and its citadel, taken from the Fatimids

ledger.note: 1025: Salih takes Aleppo. His siege began in late November 1024, the Bab Qinnasrin gate opened on 18 January 1025, the citadel was breached by 30 June 1025 and he entered it in September 1025; the Fatimid caliph al-Zahir recognised him as emir of Aleppo.

region.text: Homs, Baalbek, Sidon, Rafaniyya and Hisn Ibn Akkar

ledger.note: 1029: the Fatimids move against Salih's Syria; he is killed at al-Uqhuwana on the shore of Lake Tiberias (12 or 25 May 1029).

region.text: Sidon, Baalbek, Homs, Rafaniyya and Hisn Ibn Akkar

ledger.note: 1029: the Fatimids take the central Syrian domains. 'After the battle, the Fatimids conquered Sidon, Baalbek, Homs, Rafaniyya, and Hisn Ibn Akkar from Salih's deputies, who fled.'

region.text: Homs, Baalbek, Sidon, Rafaniyya and Hisn Ibn Akkar

ledger.note: 1029: the fight ends with the Fatimid conquest of the central Syrian domains; Nasr holds Aleppo.

1038: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa are in Numayrid hands by 1039/40; the Mirdasid page says only that the Mirdasids "had also since lost control of Raqqa and al-Rafiqa to the Numayrids" and the Nasr ibn Salih page has no dates on it (the Shabib ibn Waththab article does not exist at that title). When they were lost is on no page opened; 1038 is bridging.

1038: the Fatimid governor of Damascus takes Aleppo. 'Al-Dizbari had captured Aleppo' by June or July 1038; Nasr was killed in battle against Anushtakin; Thimal 'fled to the Jazira'. Manbij and Balis were 'lost to Anushtakin in 1038' (Mirdasid page).

1040: Thimal gains Raqqa and al-Rafiqa. 'After his brother-in-law Shabib died, Thimal's wife al-Sayyida al-Alawiyya inherited Raqqa and Rafiqa and entrusted them to him. He made Raqqa his capital.' (1039/40.) Numayrid page: Shabib died without an adult heir, "Thimal took over Raqqa", his brothers Muta'in and Qawam "jointly held Harran and Raqqa", and a long Numayr-Kilab feud over Raqqa began; no campaign is dated before April 1056, so no contest is written for 1040-1055.
1042: Thimal recovers Aleppo. 'Thimal entered Aleppo [22 February 1042] after the ahdath let him in. He took the palace quickly but needed a seven-month siege to take the citadel.'
1056: Mani' ibn Shabib of the Numayrids moves against Thimal over Raqqa. 'In April 1056, after Thimal rejected Mani's demand to withdraw from Raqqa, hostilities broke out between the two sides.'
1057: the fighting over Raqqa ends with Mani' holding it (October 1057).

1057: Raqqa and al-Rafiqa pass to the Numayrids. 'In reward, al-Basasiri captured Raqqa from Thimal and transferred it to Mani' in October 1057'; Ibn Shaddad has Thimal hand over both towns "due to military pressure"; "Thimal's surrender of Raqqa was part of a greater power shift" with the Fatimid-forced evacuation of Aleppo in January 1058. The Thimal page is silent on Raqqa after 1040 (review fix 2026-10-19).

1058: Thimal steps down and Aleppo passes to the Fatimid governor. 'Thimal stepped down on 23 January 1058' and took up residence in Cairo; in September 1060 'his nephew Mahmud ibn Nasr seized Aleppo from Ibn Mulhim'. The page does not say who held Aleppo between 1058 and 1060; Ibn Mulhim is read as the Fatimid governor. The Fatimids "compensated him with the governorships or appendages of the coastal towns of Acre, Beirut, and Jubayl (Byblos)" but this "was evidently a tributary arrangement, as he did not exercise control over them", and after September 1060 "Caliph al-Mustansir stripped Thimal of his holdings along the Syrian coast": no land gained, so no gain is written (review fix 2026-10-19).

1059: Mani' of the Numayrids takes al-Rahba. 'Mani' extended Numayrid territory to its southernmost point in 1059, taking al-Rahba and al-Qarqisiyah.' The page does not name the previous holder; the Mirdasids (Atiyya retook al-Rahba in 1061; the Thimal page says the Numayrids "had taken control of al-Rahba") are read as the loser.
1060: Mahmud ibn Nasr, the Mirdasid nephew, seizes Aleppo in September; Thimal regained it on 23 April 1061 and Atiyya gave it up to Mahmud in 1065 (internal Mirdasid succession).
1061: Atiyya retakes al-Rahba for Thimal. 'In August, Atiyya retook al-Rahba for Thimal.'
1062: Atiyya ibn Salih takes Raqqa. 'Thimal's brother, Atiyya ibn Salih, took over Raqqa in 1062'; 'In 1062, the Numayrids lost Raqqa to their distant kinsmen and erstwhile allies, the Mirdasids.'

1080: Muslim ibn Quraysh takes Aleppo. 'In 1080, prompted by Sabiq, the Uqaylid emir of Mosul, Sharaf al-Dawla Muslim, took over Aleppo.' (Uqaylid page: June 1080.) Tutush persuaded Sabiq to cede the emirate.
1080: the Mirdasid dynasty ends with the loss of Aleppo (infobox 1014-1080).

wars.name: Battle of al-Uqhuwana (Mirdasid-Fatimid war)

zones.text: Sidon, Baalbek, Homs, Rafaniyya and Hisn Ibn Akkar

wars.outcome: Salih allied with the Banu Tayy and Banu Kalb in 1023 and was killed at al-Uqhuwana on the eastern shore of Lake Tiberias in May 1029; the Fatimids took his central Syrian domains.

wars.name: Battle of Azaz
wars.outcome: Nasr "routed his forces at the Battle of Azaz (1030)" after Romanos III led the assault in person in the summer; no border moved.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Aleppo (1038)
wars.outcome: Anushtakin al-Dizbari killed Nasr in battle and seized Aleppo in summer 1038; Thimal fled to the Jazira.

wars.name: Thimal's Fatimid campaigns (1048-1050)
wars.outcome: A Fatimid army under Ibn Hamdan withdrew after flooding at Shildi in autumn 1048 (it had taken Hama earlier that year); Thimal destroyed Rifq's army at Jabal Jawshin in August 1050 and peace followed late in 1050.
wars.note: Hama's ownership before 1048 is not given, so no zone.

wars.name: Mirdasid-Numayrid war over Raqqa (1056-1057)
wars.outcome: Hostilities began in April 1056 when Thimal refused Mani's demand to leave Raqqa; Mani', backed by the Fatimid envoy al-Mu'ayyad and al-Basasiri, received Raqqa and al-Rafiqa in October 1057 (captured, or handed over under pressure per Ibn Shaddad); Atiyya ibn Salih took Raqqa back in 1062.

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Aleppo (1080)
wars.outcome: Muslim ibn Quraysh took Aleppo in June 1080 after its inhabitants offered to hand it over; the Mirdasid dynasty ended.

certainty.note: Tribal emirate of fortress towns and caravan cities; the pages give towns and no frontiers. The Lebanese coast (1025-1029) is the softest; 1059 has no drawn land.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Mirdasid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. No area on the pages (infobox none, reopened 2026-10-19). Start year follows the infobox (1014, Salih's escape); Aleppo itself was taken in 1025. Disagreements: Thimal's reign 1042-1062 (infobox) vs 'stepped down on 23 January 1058' and 1060-1061 gaps (Thimal page); Mahmud's seizure of Aleppo in 1060 is 'from Ibn Mulhim' (read as the Fatimid governor, page silent); al-Rahba taken by Salih in 1008 (Salih/Mirdasid pages) vs by Qirwash the Uqaylid in 1008/9 (Qirwash page; see uqaylid-dynasty, whose 1014 loss pairs with this dossier's found event). Not written as events: Thimal's Byzantine vassalage and Mahmud's vassalage to the Seljuk sultan (the Mirdasids are the vassal; the suzerains' dossiers carry it; both undated), Hama 1048-1050, Homs 'allotted to Nasr's emirate around 1038', the Byzantine restoration of fortresses north of Aleppo (January 1062) and the battle of Artah (May 1062). Counterparts: numayrid-dynasty (written in this batch). Gazetteer names needed: Rahba (Mayadin), Rafiqa, Balis, Rafaniyya, Hisn Ibn Akkar, Baalbek (resolved here as the Beqaa).
Review fixes (2026-10-19, author), each from a page reopened: (1) The Lebanese coast after 1058 is gone. The Thimal page: the Fatimids 'compensated him with the governorships or appendages of the coastal towns of Acre, Beirut, and Jubayl (Byblos)', 'Thimal's rule over the three coastal towns was evidently a tributary arrangement, as he did not exercise control over them', and after Mahmud took Aleppo in 1060 'Caliph al-Mustansir stripped Thimal of his holdings along the Syrian coast'. The 1058 gain event is deleted (the grant is described in the note of the 1058 Aleppo loss); Acre, Beirut and Byblos are out of every keyframe and the dissolve region (about 5,000 km2 for 22 years had no basis). (2) Raqqa now has one owner per year and numayrid-dynasty as counterpart in every event: Mirdasid from 1022 (Salih and Mirdasid pages), Numayrid from 1038 (bridging; the Mirdasid page says only 'since lost ... to the Numayrids'; the Nasr ibn Salih page has no dates; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabib_ibn_Waththab and /Shabib_ibn_Wathab are not articles, the reviewer's suggested page could not be opened), Mirdasid from 1039/40 (Thimal took it over), contested from April 1056 (Numayrid page: 'hostilities broke out'), Numayrid from October 1057 (al-Basasiri / Ibn Shaddad), Mirdasid again from 1062 (Atiyya), the pair of numayrid-dynasty's 1062 loss. Disagreement with the reviewer's suggestion (Mirdasid 1040 to 1062 with a feud contest throughout): the Numayrid page dates the transfer to Mani' to October 1057 and the first fighting to April 1056, and describes the earlier feud with no campaigns, so the contest is written for 1056-1057 only and Raqqa is Numayrid, not Mirdasid, in 1058-1061. Consequence: the Mirdasid emirate holds only al-Rahba in 1058 and no land the pages name in 1059 (al-Rahba lost to Mani'; Aleppo returns in September 1060), so 1059 has no keyframe. numayrid-dynasty (verdict fix, not touched here) still draws Raqqa Numayrid 1007-1061 without these events: it needs a loss in 1022, a gain in 1038 (bridging), a loss in 1040, a contest 1056/4-1057/10 and a gain in 1057/10 against mirdasid-dynasty, its 1062 loss already matches. (3) Capitals: Aleppo split into 1042-1057 and 1060-1080; al-Rahba added for 1038-1039 (the Thimal page: he 'retained the Mesopotamian portion', al-Dizbari 'was unable to take al-Rahba'); no capital for 1058-1059. (4) Thin items not settled: the year of Manbij and Balis (the Mirdasid page: 'In the following years' after 1014; the Salih page: 'by 1022'; stays 1015, confidence 1) and the year Raqqa left Mirdasid hands (stays 1038, confidence 1).
